text:
Jonas Weber: heads up — offline eval run from last night shows risk misclassification specifically on long-context slices (8k–16k). We’re tagging a bunch as LOW risk that should be MED/HIGH once you look at prefill latency + memory pressure.

Jonas Weber: TL;DR numbers:
- Dataset: 12 workloads (prompt sets + replay), 3 models (mixtral-ish + llama-ish), seq buckets {<=2k, 2–4k, 4–8k, 8–16k}
- Misclass rate (LOW predicted, should be >=MED): 18% overall, 31% in 8–16k bucket
- Biggest offenders: caching suggestions on routes with high prompt length variance (p95 context huge), and batching suggestions on routes where headroom calc is based on steady-state decode, not prefill

Jonas Weber: Example: `route=chat/completions`, `model=rw-open-70b`, `region=us-east`
- Risk pipeline says LOW because latency headroom computed at median ctx (~1.8k)
- But replay at 12k ctx pushes p95 prefill +1.4s and KV memory spikes → queuing instability (saw p95 end-to-end +28%)

Hassan Mirza: :eyes: do you have the confusion matrix by bucket? wondering if it’s mostly LOW->MED or LOW->HIGH.

Jonas Weber: yeah. It’s mostly LOW->MED, but there are a few LOW->HIGH when ctx p95 > 10k and request rate is bursty.

Jonas Weber: snippet from report:
- <=2k: 4% LOW misclass
- 2–4k: 9%
- 4–8k: 14%
- 8–16k: 31%

Karthik Iyer: this matches what we were worried about in the #eng-ml thread last week. we’re under-weighting variance. are we currently feeding any “context length distribution” features into risk?

Jonas Weber: only indirectly via a coarse `workload_variance_score` (based on token metering variance, not ctx length distribution). That’s part of the problem — token variance != context variance.

Selene Huang: +1. For guardrails, long-context regressions are the scary ones because they don’t show up in the “typical” p95 if the traffic mix shifts. If we’re going to keep a single LOW/MED/HIGH label, we need to be conservative when we lack coverage.

Sana Farid: are these cases also low-confidence on the savings estimate side? (i.e., baseline sample size too small in 8–16k bucket)

Jonas Weber: some are low-confidence, but not all. In a few, savings confidence is decent because overall traffic is high, but it’s skewed short-context. So the baseline is “confident” but not representative of the long-context tail.

Hassan Mirza: ok so we probably need: (a) representativeness / coverage signal, (b) explicit ctx-length features.

Jonas Weber: proposal for threshold adjustments (for ADR-0274 update / risk scorer v1.1):
1) Add `ctx_p95` (or `prefill_tokens_p95`) as a first-class feature. If `ctx_p95 >= 8192`, risk floor = MED unless we have explicit long-context eval pass.
2) Add “tail coverage” check: if long-context bucket has <N samples (suggest N=200 req/day or >=5% traffic share), bump risk by +1 level (LOW->MED, MED->HIGH). Call it “insufficient long-context telemetry”.
3) Update latency headroom calculation to use bucketed headroom (compute headroom at ctx_p95, not ctx_median). If bucketed headroom < 15%, bump risk.

Jonas Weber: also propose UI rationale bullet to explicitly say why: “High prompt-length variance / long-context tail may increase prefill latency” instead of the current generic “workload variance”.

Logan Wright: telemetry side: we can expose ctx length distribution per route/model pretty easily (we already have input_tokens histograms in metering). But bucketed headroom at ctx_p95 might require joining with latency histograms by token bucket — we have some of that but it’s not wired into the suggestions dataset yet.

Chloe Martin: from Console POV, if risk becomes “MED by default when ctx_p95 >= 8k”, we need to make sure we don’t spam customers with MED/HIGH and kill trust. Can we gate with “only if suggestion touches batching/caching parameters that affect prefill/queueing”?

Jonas Weber: fair. The misclass we saw is almost entirely on (a) caching config changes (prefix caching on/off, cache TTL changes) and (b) batching aggressiveness. So we can scope the conservative rule to those suggestion types.

Karthik Iyer: what about decode-only routes (short prompt, long output) — does this change anything?

Jonas Weber: didn’t see issues there. This is prefill dominated. For decode-heavy, current headroom features were ok.

Selene Huang: for beta guardrails, I’d be comfortable with “risk floor = MED when ctx_p95 >= 8k AND no eval coverage” even if it means fewer LOWs. Better to be conservative in beta.

Sana Farid: re: confidence intervals: we should avoid mixing “risk” and “confidence”, but we can incorporate the coverage signal as a risk factor (since it increases uncertainty of impact). I can help define the threshold for “insufficient tail coverage” so it’s not arbitrary.

Yara Haddad: implementation-wise, easiest path:
- add new fields to risk scorer input payload (ctx_p95, ctx_bucket_counts)
- calibrate a small set of rules first (your 3), then we can revisit model-based calibration later

Hassan Mirza: +1 rules-first. We can iterate fast and it’s explainable.

Jonas Weber: action items:
- I’ll open a ticket for risk scorer v1.1 threshold change + new ctx features (cc @Yara Haddad @Logan Wright)
- @Sana Farid can you suggest numbers for tail coverage thresholds (N, traffic share) by EOD?
- @Selene Huang can you sanity check the “risk floor” rule vs guardrails doc? want to ensure it matches how we suppress recs.

Chloe Martin: pls also tag me when the input contract changes — we’ll need to make sure the UI rationale bullets have the new fields. :thumbsup:

Logan Wright: re telemetry join, I’ll check if we can get ctx histograms into the suggestions dataset without blowing up cardinality. Might do it as percentiles only (p50/p95/p99) rather than full hist.

Jonas Weber: sounds good. attaching the eval summary link here: <https://redwood-internal/wiki/suggestions/evals/2024-03-17-long-context-risk|offline eval summary (long-context risk)> (WIP, will clean up)

Hassan Mirza: thanks. those 31% numbers are… not great. glad we caught before beta expands.

Selene Huang: :+1: better now than after a customer asks “why did you say LOW risk and my p95 blew up”.

Jonas Weber: exactly. I’ll post an update once we rerun with the rules to see how much it reduces misclass.
